candidates.name: queue — A synchronized queue class
verified_facts: Provides synchronized queues, task accounting, blocking retrieval, task_done, and join coordination.
semantic_limits: Queue size is approximate and queue emptiness does not prove all external side effects are complete.

candidates.name: multiprocessing — Process-based parallelism
verified_facts: Provides child-process lifecycle, start methods, pools, queues, pipes, synchronization, and process identity.
semantic_limits: Child existence does not prove canonical ownership; parent, command, start method, PID, start time, and outputs must match.

candidates.name: contextlib — Utilities for with-statement contexts
verified_facts: Provides context managers and utilities for deterministic setup, cleanup, redirection, and stack-based resource management.
semantic_limits: A context manager cannot guarantee external durability or cleanup when the process is forcibly terminated.

candidates.name: asyncio — Asynchronous I/O
verified_facts: Provides event loops, tasks, synchronization, subprocess and stream integration, and timeout primitives.
semantic_limits: A scheduled coroutine or running loop does not prove task progress without state and artifact readback.

candidates.name: logging — Logging facility for Python
verified_facts: Provides loggers, levels, handlers, formatters, filters, exception information, and structured LogRecord fields.
semantic_limits: Log records can be buffered, filtered, reordered, or forged and are not sufficient as receipts without hashes and state readback.

candidates.name: logging.handlers — Logging handlers
verified_facts: Provides file, rotating, watched, queue, network, buffering, and memory handlers.
semantic_limits: Handler success does not prove data reached stable storage; flush, close, rotation, path, and file hash must be verified.

candidates.name: faulthandler — Dump the Python traceback
verified_facts: Can dump Python tracebacks explicitly, on faults, or after a timeout through a watchdog thread.
semantic_limits: Traceback dumping diagnoses stalls but does not repair them, and its output descriptor must remain valid.

candidates.name: tracemalloc — Trace memory allocations
verified_facts: Traces Python memory allocations and supports snapshots, statistics, filters, and snapshot comparison.
semantic_limits: Allocation traces cover Python-managed allocations and do not establish process liveness or task completion.

candidates.name: traceback — Print or retrieve a stack traceback
verified_facts: Formats and extracts exceptions, stacks, exception groups, and chained exception context.
semantic_limits: A formatted traceback is diagnostic text and must be correlated with exact process, code, time, and failing input.

candidates.name: warnings — Warning control
verified_facts: Provides warning categories, filters, emission, capture, and logging integration.
semantic_limits: Warnings are not failures by default and their absence does not prove correctness.

candidates.name: json — JSON encoder and decoder
verified_facts: Provides JSON serialization, parsing, custom encoders and decoders, and command-line validation support.
semantic_limits: Syntactically valid JSON does not prove schema, identity, order, freshness, or semantic correctness.

candidates.name: configparser — Configuration file parser
verified_facts: Parses INI-style configuration with sections, defaults, interpolation, converters, and configurable strictness.
semantic_limits: Parsed values may inherit defaults or interpolation and must be normalized before identity comparisons.

candidates.name: hashlib — Secure hashes and message digests
verified_facts: Provides SHA-2, SHA-3, BLAKE2 and other digest constructors plus file_digest for file hashing.
semantic_limits: A matching digest proves byte equality for the selected algorithm, not provenance, authorization, or freshness.
